Use the TA-10 flagger setup, since a one-lane closure on a two-lane road needs a flagger at each end (Figure 6P-10).

1. Advance signs each way: ROAD WORK AHEAD, ONE LANE ROAD AHEAD, then the Flagger sign, spaced from Table 6B-1.
2. Flagger at each end, lit at night, with a 50 to 100 ft one-lane two-way taper of cones about 20 ft apart.
3. Leave a buffer space if there is room, then cones along the work at no more than 90 ft apart (2 x 45 mph).
4. Finish with a downstream taper, set up with traffic, and take down in reverse.

- Your competent person decides on site.

Want the rest: Table 6B-1 sign spacing at 45 mph and the approved plan?

OSHA requires Type B soil to be sloped no steeper than 1:1 (45°) for excavations 20 feet or less deep (Appendix B, Table B-1).
- Instead of sloping: a trench box or shield, timber or aluminum hydraulic shoring, or an engineered design (1926.652(b)-(c)).
- Benching in Type B is also allowed at a maximum 1:1 slope, with set bench dimensions.
- Your competent person decides on site.

Want the rest: bench dimensions and the vertical-lower-side rule?

The entry supervisor authorizes entry and signs the permit only after every condition on it is met (29 CFR 1910.146).

1. Name the entry supervisor, attendant and entrants, with their duties and training (1926.1204).
2. Isolate the line and set up ventilation, communication, retrieval and rescue.
3. Test the air before entry: O2, LEL, H2S and CO.
4. Fill in the permit with the test results, hazards and rescue arrangements.
5. The entry supervisor signs; keep monitoring while anyone is inside.
6. Cancel the permit when work ends or conditions change.

- Your competent person decides on site.

Want the rest: the permit's required contents and the atmosphere limits?

Disinfect the new main under AWWA C651, using the method your spec names. Then flush, dechlorinate, and pass bac-T samples before connecting.

1. Keep the pipe clean while laying, with plugs in open ends and no trench water in the pipe.
2. Fill slowly through a backflow-protected connection with chlorine at 25 mg/L, held 24 hours.
3. At the end, at least 10 mg/L free chlorine must remain.
4. Flush to system levels, dechlorinate the discharge, and take bac-T samples.
5. Don't connect until two sample sets pass.

Want the rest: tablet and slug methods, and bac-T sample timing?

Here is the most common case, an AWWA C605 hydrostatic test on a PVC main:
1. Restrain bends, tees and plugs with blocks or restrained joints first, and brace temporary caps.
2. Fill slowly and bleed all air at hydrants, air valves and taps.
3. Raise to test pressure, commonly 1.5 times working pressure or 150 psi minimum, or your spec's number.
4. Hold at least 2 hours, pumping make-up water to keep pressure.
5. Leakage allowed is L = S x D x sqrt(P) / 148,000 gal/hr; 1,000 ft of 8 in at 150 psi is 0.66 gal/hr.
6. Pressure that keeps dropping usually means air, a passing valve, or a leaking joint or tap.

Want the rest: disinfection, flushing and bac-T sampling after the test?

The construction permit (29 CFR 1926.1206) must identify the space, purpose, date and duration, entrants, attendants, entry supervisor, hazards, isolation measures, acceptable conditions, test results, rescue, communications, equipment, and other permits.

1. The space, purpose of entry, date and authorized duration.
2. Entrants (by name or roster), attendants and entry supervisor (names, supervisor's signature or initials).
3. Hazards, isolation and control measures, and acceptable entry conditions.
4. Test results with tester's name or initials and time.
5. Rescue and emergency services, how to summon them, and communication procedures.
6. Equipment (PPE, testing, alarms, rescue), other safety information, and other permits such as hot work.

- Your competent person decides on site.

Want the rest: signing, posting and retention rules for the permit?

You must give pedestrians a reasonably safe, accessible temporary walkway or detour, signed ahead so no one walks up to a dead end (MUTCD Part 6, 6C.02).

1. Post SIDEWALK CLOSED AHEAD CROSS HERE (R9-11) before the closure, and SIDEWALK CLOSED (R9-9) at it.
2. Send people across at an intersection, not mid-block.
3. Span the full closed width with a cane-detectable barrier; no tape, rope or cones alone.
4. Keep the temporary route accessible, with ramps 12:1 or flatter.
5. Cover or fence the open trench next to the walkway.

- Your competent person decides on site.

Want the rest: widths, ramp landings, edging heights and the traffic control permit?

No. OSHA's Type C soil has no benching option in Appendix B; Type C allows only simple slopes (1 1/2:1 max) or a shielded or supported vertical lower portion (29 CFR 1926 Subpart P, App. B, B-1.3). Texas follows federal OSHA for private crews.
- Benching in Type C would need an engineer's design or tabulated data under 1926.652(b)(3) or (b)(4).
- A shield or support must extend at least 18 inches above the vertical side.
- Your competent person decides on site.

Want the rest: how benching works in Type A and B soil?

For a 55 mph highway (rural or high-speed), the MUTCD spacing table gives about 500 ft between advance warning signs, and 1,000 / 1,500 / 2,640 ft on an expressway or freeway [5].
- The approved traffic control plan or permit governs, so follow its spacing.
- Arkansas's manual edition and sign spacing are not confirmed; ask the ARDOT traffic office [1].
- Your competent person decides on site.

Want the rest: taper length, buffer space and cone spacing at 55 mph?

OSHA requires the box to be selected under the manufacturer's tabulated data, used within every limit the manufacturer sets for the classified soil type and depth (29 CFR 1926.652(c)(2)).
- The data sheet must be at the jobsite, and any deviation needs the manufacturer's written approval.
- Check the box's depth rating for your soil type, the surcharge limit and the spreader lengths against 12 ft.
- Your competent person decides on site.

This is the federal rule. The library has no Tennessee rule for it, so confirm with Tennessee's OSHA plan.
